title: arXiv AI: latest announcement batch — 11 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this inferred ordering is a relevance-led shortlist, not a measured popularity ranking. The batch is very recent and citation evidence is too limited to establish popularity.

sections.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
sections.abstract: ReTrace converts SOPs and a few reasoning-and-tool-call traces into executable workflows where code chooses each next step, reporting lower runtime cost and latency with a small completion trade-off on its tested procedures.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors extract action conditions and input sources from agent reasoning and tool records, merge them into evidence-linked rules, and compile these into executable workflows; results cover one production platform and two benchmarks.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say recovered conditions are not proven correct by their construction checks; their evaluation tests new inputs to the same procedures, not transfer to new procedures, and the public tests cover only the telecom tau-squared-Bench domain and eight SOP-Bench domains.

sections.title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
sections.abstract: FGSE represents proposed agent-memory updates as hypotheses and tests transfer, counterexamples, and regression risk before committing them, reporting results across web, app, tool-use, and long-term-memory benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a verifier-grounded commit/refine/reject gate for persistent memory updates and report reduced harmful committed updates alongside benchmark performance.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors frame extension to multimodal agents and settings where verifiers must be learned or approximated as future work; the reported approach assumes verifier-rich environments.

sections.title: A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets
sections.abstract: The paper analyzes how policy-gradient updates can lose access to high-reward responses even as reward rises, then gives coverage-preserving convergence guarantees for methods that periodically reset their KL reference.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors define coverage-preserving policy optimization, describe a coverage-collapse failure for REINFORCE, and use Approximate Policy Mirror Descent/reference resets to prove global convergence for stylized PPO/GRPO and squared-loss families under stated assumptions.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors limit end-to-end guarantees to softmax linear policies over pretrained features and a one-shot response setting; richer policies, token-sequence effects, and multi-step reasoning remain open.

sections.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
sections.abstract: AutoScaffold uses a frozen teacher to adapt strategies and hints from a student's RL training experience, then evaluates the student without those scaffolds across four domains.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that students trained with adaptive strategy-level and task-level hints outperform corresponding RL baselines after the hints are removed, with reported gains in ALFWorld, QA, math, and GPU-kernel generation.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are limited to the four tested domains and the teacher-guided training setup; the reported comparisons do not establish transfer to broader, unseen training regimes.

sections.title: ARE-bench: Benchmarking Agents' Research Ability in Real-World Researcher Sessions and Workspaces
sections.abstract: ARE-bench tests whether research agents can make progress on ongoing projects while respecting prior decisions and messy existing workspaces, using 75 tasks drawn from real researcher sessions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce an evaluation set preserving prior session requirements and workspace state; they report that the strongest of seven evaluated models passes every checklist item on 66.2% of tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper evaluates one curated set of 75 tasks from recruited researchers' projects; performance on this dataset does not by itself establish reliability across disciplines or new project environments.

sections.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
sections.abstract: This study compares trace-based judging, text-only judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics on two analytics agents, measuring repeatability, known-risk detection, and discovery of new failures.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors find trace-based judging has the strongest precision-recall balance on their known-risk set and recommend combining trace-based functional evaluation with adversarial red-teaming.
sections.unique_caveat: The experiment covers two analytics agents in a controlled setting using frozen traces, so its relative framework results may not transfer unchanged to other agent types or live environments.

sections.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
sections.abstract: WikiTrace links each stored lesson to its supporting trajectory and lets an agent retrieve that evidence when a lesson is incomplete, conflicting, or based on failure; the authors report gains across five agentic benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine concise memory insights with summaries and raw trajectories, enabling tool-assisted evidence checks before acting; they report reduced memory-induced degradation relative to memory baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: The method depends on retaining and retrieving the source trajectory for each insight; the abstract reports evaluation on five agentic benchmarks, not unrestricted deployment settings.

sections.title: REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding
sections.abstract: REAL derives an unbiased, variance-reduced loss for training speculative-decoding draft models against the actual token-acceptance process rather than surrogate distribution-overlap objectives.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author derives path-weighted REAL with Rao-Blackwellization and reports higher probabilistic serving acceptance length than four compared losses in the tested Qwen3.6-35B-A3B/Domino setup.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evaluation is a controlled loss-level comparison for one target/drafter configuration; it does not establish the same gains across other architectures or serving workloads.
